title: Sola fide is not idle faith apart from works—only living faith justifies
source_text: XXVIII. Praeterea, quando cum Paulo asserimus, hominem justificari sola fide & sine operibus, ex ante dictis satis patet, ab eo nos multum abesse, ut sentiamus fidem quae sola est, & seorsim a bonis operibus existit, vim habere justificandi. Siquidem non aliam fidem justificantem agnoscimus, quam quae viva est, & ex se bona opera producit.
pass_a_gloss: Further, when with Paul we assert that a person is justified by faith alone and without works, from what was said before it is clear enough that we are far from thinking that faith which is alone and exists apart from good works has power to justify. For we acknowledge no other justifying faith than that which is living and from itself produces good works.
pass_b_english: Sola fide does not mean idle faith severed from works can justify.
Only living faith that itself produces good works is justifying faith.

choices.why: Idle solitary faith is not justifying.
